name: Option 4 — Leadership (Moderation Guide)
reference_usage: Visual language shared with /research-plan Option 4; the runtime does not require access to any private reference document. page/colors/typography/warning/spacing tokens are copied verbatim from the research-plan contract so the finished look matches. The document structure is inferred generically (structure-agnostic) and each table's geometry is derived from its own column count and first header cell.
supported_guide_shapes: Interview / IDI (two-tier header, extended RACI, prose-bullet themes with indented probes, Participants Log / Parking Lot table after the debrief)
Prototype / Usability (single breadcrumb, Session Flow Overview, '#|Ask' & '#|Ask / Do' task tables under '### Flow N', vendor Communication & Deliverables back-matter after the debrief)

breadcrumb._note: Styles a single breadcrumb line AND the interview two-tier header (all-caps kicker above the title + the italic period line below it). Any short pre-title line and the interview period line render at this breadcrumb level.

phase_subtitle._note: Optional bold subtitle line under the title (dark-green-on-white, distinct from the white-on-green band).

heading._note: Inherited research-plan token; intentionally UNUSED in mod-guide. Its structural role is taken by the 14pt section bands.

section_band._note: Applied to EVERY Heading-2, generically (Research Objectives, Prototype Tasks, Wrap-Up, Post-Session Debrief, Participants Log, Parking Lot, Communication & Deliverables, …).

sub_phase_heading._note: Applied to EVERY Heading-3 (e.g. 'Flow 1', '2.1'); green-on-white so it never reads as a band. Alt: DM Sans 11pt bold #003D29.

context_note._note: Used for the optional 'Last updated' metadata line.

structure.role_inference: generic — title = first H1; breadcrumb/kicker = short pre-title line(s) or the italic period line after the title; RACI = consecutive '**Label:** …' bullets (any label set); warning = the TEST ARTIFACT paragraph; every H2 = band; every H3 = sub-phase; every table = Option 4 table styling; every list preserves nesting; all other paragraphs = body.
structure.no_terminal_section: The guide may end anywhere (a table may appear after Post-Session Debrief). The formatter does NOT enforce a terminal section — that content rule lives in SKILL.md / the templates.

section_bands.applies_to: every ## heading in the document, generically; labels adapt to the study, do not copy an old study's wording

tables.border: MIRROR research-plan option4_layout.py; single thin neutral border, consistent across all tables; the base Option 4 contract defines no border color/weight, so this is the sole value to confirm against the research-plan builder rather than invent.
tables.column_width_rule: The first column is narrow (90pt) when the first header cell is '#' (question/task tables), otherwise it uses the label width (144pt). The remaining width is split evenly across the other columns so every table's outer edge aligns at total_width_pt. Examples: 2-col '#|Ask' -> [90, 608.4]; 2-col Parameter|Detail / Cue|Read aloud / Time|Phase -> [144, 554.4]; 3-col Date & Time|Panelist Bio|Recording -> [144, 277.2, 277.2].
tables.label_background_rule: A two-column table in the top matter (the Parameter|Detail dashboard) gets the gray label column so it reads as an at-a-glance dashboard; every in-section table (consent, question/task, Session Flow Overview, Participants Log, Timeline, …) uses a white label column.
tables.first_column_bold_rule: The first (label) column renders bold when EVERY first cell in the source Markdown is fully bold (Parameter|Detail, Cue|Read aloud, #|Ask). Tables whose first column is not uniformly bold (e.g. a Participants Log's Date & Time values) render the first column at normal weight; inline emphasis from the source is honored either way.

optional_header_row.note: The Markdown header row is treated as a conversion header and dropped on import (the first content row becomes the first visible row). Header presence is detected per table by row count, so a table may or may not arrive with the header still attached.
